title: Revolt of Keis ibn Mekshuh and murder of Daduweihi in the Yemen
description: Keis ibn Mekshuh, unwilling to serve under the Persian Feiruz, plotted to expel the foreign settlers and called in 'Amr ibn Ma'dikerib, a poet and chief who had cast off the Faith. Daduweihi was treacherously slain by 'Amr at a feast; Feiruz escaped to a friendly tribe, his family was taken captive, and the Persian settlers fled to the mountains or took ship from Aden. Dated to the year 0632 by the source.

sources.citation: Sir William Muir, The Caliphate: Its Rise, Decline, and Fall, "II A.H. 632-633 A.D."
